 Judgment

The present appeal is filed by the appellant-claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 05.02.2015 in MVC.No.3552/2012 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru, for seeking enhancement of compensation.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts of the case are that, on 06.05.2012 at about 10.30 pm., the driver of Tempo 407 bearing Reg.No.KA-40-1142 drove the same slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road and when he reached near Kurubarakunte gate, Vijayapura Devanahalli road, Devanahalli Taluk, at that time, Eicher Canter bearing Reg.NO.KA-51-8285 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Tempo 407 bearing Reg.No.KA-40- 1142.
Due to which, the claimant sustained several grievous injuries.

3. Heard the arguments from both sides and perused the records.
4.

The Tribunal has awarded the compensation under various heads as follows:

sentences.text:
7. Learned counsel for respondent No.1-Insurance Company submitted that the claimant had suffered only simple injuries as per Ex.P.4- wound certificate issued by Deeksha Hospital,
Bengaluru, but as per Ex.P.6-discharge summary issued by Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics Hospital, Bengaluru, it is stated that the claimant had suffered upper 3rd both bones of right leg.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics Hospital, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Hence, suspected that the claimant had suffered fractured injuries to the leg.

Therefore,
submitted that the claimant had only suffered simple injuries.
Further more, Ex.P.6- discharge summary does not contain the seal of the hospital and the doctor is not examined.
Also the X-ray film to show the fracture is caused is not produced before the Tribunal.
Therefore, suspected that the claimant had suffered fractured injuries as contended.

8. Even though, in Ex.P.4-wound certificate issued by the Deeksha Hospital, the injuries stated is deep lacerated cut wound on head and small abrasion over back/palm and it is stated as simple in nature.
But soon after the accident, the claimant has firstly gone to the Deeksha Hospital and then to Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics Hospital, Bengaluru.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics Hospital, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Therefore, there is no time gap between the accident and admitted to the hospital.

May be Deeksha Hospital has not stated sustaining of grievous injuries, but the Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics Hospital, Bengaluru, stated that the claimant had suffered fracture to the right leg.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics Hospital, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The claimant has undergone surgery in the Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics Hospital, Bengaluru.

sentences.text: Since there is no time gap between the date of accident and admitted to the Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics Hospital, Bengaluru, after taking primary treatment in Deeksha Hospital, therefore, the evidence of Ex.P.6- discharge summary issued by Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics Hospital, Bengaluru can be believed.

sentences.text: Accordingly, compensation of Rs.10,000/- granted under the head pain and suffering is on the lesser side and the same is enhanced to Rs.40,000/-.
10. The compensation of Rs.20,000/- awarded under the head medical expenses is as per the actual bills produced.
Hence, it is kept in tact.
11. Further compensation of Rs.10,000/- awarded under the head food, nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges is on the lesser side.
It is stated that the claimant was admitted in the hospital for a period of 23 days.
Accordingly, compensation of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under the said head.

12. Further compensation of Rs.21,000/- (Rs.7,000/- pm., x 3 months) is awarded under the head loss of income during laid up period by considering the monthly income as Rs.7,000/- for a period of three months.
13. The Tribunal has not awarded compensation under the head loss of amenities.

Hence,
compensation of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under the head loss of amenities.

14. Thus, in all, the appellant/claimant is entitled to the compensation as follows:
1 Pain and suffering Rs. 40,000/- 2 Medical expenses Rs. 20,000/- Kept in tact 3 Food, nourishment, Rs.
25,000/-
Conveyance and Attendant charges 4 Loss of income during the Rs. 21,000/- period of treatment 5 Loss of amenities Rs. 25,000/-
Total Rs
15. The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.50,000/-, but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.1,31,000/-.
Hence, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.81,000/- (Rs.1,31,000/- - Rs.50,000/-).

Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.81,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
Regarding pay and recovery:
16. In the present case, the accident was caused on 06.05.2012.
The driver of Eicher Canter had possessed the driving licence till 05.05.2012.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident, the driver did not have the driving licence.
Therefore, it is proved that there is no licence.
Hence, the Insurance Company has established its defence as per Sub-section (2) of Section 147 of MV Act.
